title: NIVXTIME
tagline: Full-stack entertainment venue platform: Flutter app, marketing site, admin dashboard, and WhatsApp automation.
overview: NIVXTIME is the most architecturally complete system I've built: a Flutter customer app, a Next.js marketing site, a Laravel API, a React admin dashboard, and a WhatsApp automation layer, all working together for an entertainment venue business.
problem: The business needed customers to discover and book activities online, staff to manage bookings and inventory from a dashboard, and automated WhatsApp updates — without stitching together disconnected third-party tools.
solution: I built the system as a coordinated monorepo: a Flutter app for customer bookings, a Next.js site for public marketing and discovery, a Laravel API as the single source of truth, a React dashboard for staff operations, and an Evolution API integration for automated WhatsApp notifications.
architecture: Laravel API at the core, consumed by three separate frontends (Flutter, Next.js, React dashboard) so each interface stays focused on its audience instead of becoming a bloated all-in-one app. WhatsApp automation runs as a separate service triggered by backend events.
features: Customer-facing Flutter app for browsing and booking activities
Public Next.js marketing site for discovery and information
Staff dashboard for managing bookings, inventory, and schedules
Automated WhatsApp notifications for booking confirmations and updates
Dockerized services for consistent deployment across environments
challenges: Keeping four separate applications (app, site, dashboard, automation) in sync against one evolving API contract
Integrating WhatsApp automation reliably without it becoming a single point of failure for bookings
Structuring the monorepo so each piece could be developed and deployed independently
lessonsLearned: A shared API contract, documented early, is what actually keeps a multi-frontend system from drifting apart
Automation layers (like WhatsApp) should degrade gracefully — the core booking flow has to work even if automation is down
futureImprovements: Shared TypeScript/Dart type definitions generated from a single API schema
Real-time booking availability using WebSockets instead of polling
results: A single coordinated system covering customer booking, staff operations, and automated communication
